title: What the game writes down for you
target: How TCG Card Shop Simulator records a shop: which parts are saved by kind, which lists hold what the shop shows and owns, and why an inventory points at those lists instead of holding its own numbers.
version: no version stated by this build (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A shop with shelves and stock in it
A moment before changing the layout

steps.do: Know that your shop is written down by kind rather than as one block, because each kind of shelf has a save record of its own.
steps.because: each kind of shelf has its own save record (CardShelfSaveData, CardStorageShelfSaveData, ShelfSaveData, WarehouseShelfSaveData)

steps.do: Expect a shelf that holds cards and products together to be recorded separately, because it has a record of its own.
steps.because: a shelf that holds cards and items together keeps a record of its own (CardItemCombiShelfSaveData)

steps.do: Remember what the machines were doing, because the automatic pack opener is saved as well.
steps.because: the automatic pack opener is saved as well (AutoPackOpenerSaveData)

steps.do: Do not unpack boxes before saving if you care about what is inside them, because packaging boxes keep their own record.
steps.because: packaging boxes have a save record of their own (PackageBoxCardSaveData)

steps.do: Expect the people to be written down too, because customers are saved as records of their own.
steps.because: customers are written down as records of their own (CustomerSaveData)

steps.do: Save deliberately rather than by quitting, because saving and loading has a panel of its own with a slot index and a save control.
steps.because: saving and loading has a panel of its own with a slot index and a save control (SaveLoadSlotPanelUI, m_SlotIndex, m_SaveBtn)

steps.do: Know that one list holds the shop's own objects, furniture and decorations, split by the surface they go on.
steps.because: one data object holds objects, furniture and decorations split by surface (ShelfData_ScriptableObject, m_ObjectDataList, m_FurniturePurchaseDataList, m_DecoDataList, m_FloorDecoDataList, m_WallDecoDataList, m_WallBarDecoDataList, m_CeilingDecoDataList, m_PosterDecoList, m_OtherDecoList)

steps.do: Know that another list decides what your shop puts on show, including accessories, figurines and board games.
steps.because: another object holds what the shop shows, including item kinds, accessories, figurines and board games (StockItemData_ScriptableObject, m_ShownItemType, m_ShownAccessoryItemType, m_ShownFigurineItemType, m_ShownBoardGameItemType)

steps.do: Look there for the card side as well: which sets and collection packs are shown, and the list of card packs.
steps.because: it also holds which card sets and collection packs are shown, and a list of card packs (m_ShownCardExpansionType, m_ShownCollectionPackType, m_CardPackItemTypeList)

steps.do: Expect restock and event data to live on the same object rather than in separate files.
steps.because: the restock data and the game event data are kept in the same object (m_RestockDataList, m_GameEventDataList)

steps.do: Check the cost multipliers there before planning upgrades, because shelf unlock and upgrade costs are values on it.
steps.because: the shelf unlock and upgrade cost multipliers are values on it (m_ShelfUnlockCostMultiplier, m_ShelfUpgradeCostMultiplier)

steps.do: Remember that images are held as lists too, and that an inventory points at these objects rather than holding its own numbers.
steps.because: it carries image lists and an inventory points at the data objects rather than holding the values itself (m_MaleCustomerIconList, m_FemaleCustomerIconList, m_PlayerIcon, m_AncientArtifactSpriteList, m_CollectionPackImageSpriteList, InventoryBase, m_StockItemData_SO, m_MonsterData_SO, m_ObjectData_SO, m_TextSO)

commonMistakes: Quitting instead of saving, when the game has a save panel with a slot and a control of its own.
Being surprised by a box's contents after a reload, when packaging boxes have their own record.
Looking for the shop's lists in several files when they live on two data objects.
Planning a shelf upgrade without looking at the cost multipliers the data carries.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. The grounding for each step is listed on the technical reference pages; nothing here is estimated.
